 Stephen Curry, Brandin Podziemski, Will Richard, Yaxel Lendeborg and Draymond Green will start Monday’s game against the Suns. 
 Curry and Green are back after sitting out Sunday’s win over the Clippers. Also, Richard will make his first start of the season. De’Anthony Melton, Georges Niang and Charles Bassey are available off the bench after starting on Sunday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Brandon Williams (quad) has been ruled out against the Suns on Monday. 
 Williams will be unavailable on the second night of this back-to-back. He has been a reliable source of offense for the Warriors this season as the backup point guard. Gary Payton II and Will Richard should take on extra minutes in his absence. 
 Yaxel Lendeborg 
 GSW 
 Forward 
 #1 
 Yaxel Lendeborg (foot) is questionable for Wednesday’s matchup with the Timberwolves. 
 Lendeborg has been Golden State’s best player through the first week of the season, and his 31/12/6 line on Monday led to an upset road win over the Nuggets. If Lendeborg is forced to sit out against Minnesota, Will Richard and Georges Niang could see more run, but neither carry much streaming appeal for fantasy hoops. 
 Brandon Williams 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #12 
 Brandon Williams tallied 20 points (5-of-10 FGs, 8-of-11 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, two steals and two three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Suns. 
 With Stephen Curry and Brandin Podziemski sitting out the second game of Golden State’s back-to-back, Williams and Will Richard (11 points, one assist, two steals, one block and three three-pointers) were inserted into the starting lineup on Saturday. After shooting 4-of-17 in Golden State’s first two games, Williams was much more efficient against the Suns. His fantasy value will depend on the schedule going forward, and the Warriors end their four-game Week 2 with another back-to-back. 
 Brandon Williams 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #12 
 Brandon Williams, Will Richard, Gui Santos, Yaxel Lendeborg and Graham Ike will start Saturday’s game against the Suns. 
 Stephen Curry, Brandin Podziemski and Draymond Green are all unavailable after starting Friday’s loss to the Grizzlies. They’ve been replaced in the starting lineup by Williams, Richard and Santos. Given the absences, all three are worth streaming in deep leagues, while Yaxel Lendeborg should already be rostered in standard leagues. 
 Stephen Curry 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #30 
 Stephen Curry (knee) is out for Saturday’s game against the Suns. 
 No surprise here as Curry said after Friday’s loss to the Grizzlies that he probably wouldn’t play against the Suns Saturday. With Brandin Podziemski also out, De’Anthony Melton and Will Richard could start and see significant minutes. 
 Will Richard 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Will Richard amassed 15 points (3-of-7 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, one steal and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s exhibition against the Trail Blazers. 
 As a rookie, Richard averaged 20.0 minutes per appearance and shot 33.5 percent from beyond the arc. With Jimmy Butler III and Moses Moody both out recovering from knee injuries, Richard will have opportunities to earn more playing time. He started against the Trail Blazers, as the Warriors rested many key contributors in the second game of a back-to-back. Despite his showing in Portland, Richard isn’t a must-draft player, especially in 12-team formats. 
 Brandon Williams 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #10 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that Brandon Williams has agreed to a one-year, $2.6 million deal to join the Golden State Warriors. 
 In his third season with Dallas, Williams enjoyed the most productive campaign of his career behind averages of 13 points, 2.9 rebounds, 2.9 assists and 1.2 “stocks.” He’ll offer depth to a Warriors team that surprisingly stood pat during free agency, and Williams will compete for backup guard minutes with the likes of De’Anthony Melton and Will Richard. 
 Will Richard 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Will Richard totaled 16 points (6-of-8 FGs), three rebounds, three assists, three steals and four three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Lakers. 
 Richard looked on Friday like someone who’d logged legitimate NBA minutes before. He shot the ball efficiently, did some nice secondary playmaking, and was active defensively with his hands. But one of the most important takeaways from the contest was how productive Richard was from beyond the arc. He shot 4-of-5 from deep, which is big, considering the 33.5 percent of three-pointers he made last season as a rookie. If he can remain consistent from the three-point line, Richard should be able to find a bigger role next season on a team that currently has limited backcourt depth. 
 Will Richard 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Will Richard (back) is available for Sunday’s game against the Clippers. 
 Richard is good to go for Sunday’s regular-season finale. With the Warriors locked into the No. 10 seed in the West, the rookie wing may play extended minutes if his back holds up. 
 Draymond Green 
 GSW 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Draymond Green (back) and Will Richard (back) are questionable for Saturday’s game against the Clippers. 
 While both were available for Friday’s loss to the Kings, Richard was limited to three minutes off the bench while Green started and logged 24. If Richard can’t play, his minutes can be absorbed by the Warriors’ other perimeter reserves, such as De’Anthony Melton and Pat Spencer. A void left by Green would be more challenging to fill, with Gary Payton II being one of the options.

 Cameron Johnson finished with seven points (2-of-5 FGs), four rebounds, two assists, two steals and one three-pointer against the Trail Blazers on Monday.
 Johnson checked out of this game with 1:08 remaining after appearing to tweak something in his left leg. Head coach David Adelman didn’t have an update after the game, so there isn’t any conclusion to draw at this point, other than Johnson could be hurt and miss time. If that happens, Trevon Brazile or Alpha Diallo will likely step into a starting role in place of Johnson.

 Nikola Jokić posted a full line on Monday with 26 points (10-of-22 FGs), nine rebounds, eight assists, four steals, one block and two three-pointers against the Trail Blazers.
 Jokić simply hasn’t been as effective this season. It’s early, and he’ll turn it around, but he just hasn’t been the same player. However, that isn’t true in fantasy basketball. He has made up for a dip in points, rebounds, assists and field goal percentage with a bump in steals, blocks and free throw percentage. Frankly, none of that is sustainable. All of it will likely regulate, with Jokić still ending up as one of the best players in fantasy basketball. Just be patient. He’ll look to stuff the stat sheet against the Raptors on Wednesday.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Lauri Markkanen had 22 points (8-of-16 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists, one steal and four three-pointers against the Spurs on Monday. 
 Markkanen’s 22 points were a game-high, though the Jazz still lost by 22 to the Spurs. He bounced back nicely after scoring just 13 points on 14 attempts in Saturday’s loss to the Trail Blazers. Markkanen and the Jazz have three more games this week with their next matchup against the Pelicans on the road Wednesday. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Jamal Murray 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #27 
 Player Stats

 Jamal Murray led the Nuggets with 35 points (10-of-19 FGs, 11-of-11 FTs), five rebounds, six assists, one block and four three-pointers in a 118-110 loss to the Trail Blazers on Monday.
 Murray has been on a tear since the season opener. He was held to just six points in that game but has averaged 31.6 points, 6.2 assists, 1.2 steals and 5.4 triples while shooting 52.1 percent from the floor and 52.9 percent from deep in their five games since. This was his third game with at least 35 points in that stretch, and while it wasn’t enough for them to win, he continues to be a fantasy star and will look to stay hot against the Raptors on Wednesday.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Jrue Holiday provided a boost off the bench with 17 points (7-of-11 FGs), eight rebounds, 10 assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers against the Nuggets on Monday.
 Holiday didn’t step into the starting unit when Ja Morant (hamstring) went down, but he did step up off the bench in this game. He fell shy of the triple-double, but he did set season highs for both rebounds and assists in the win. Portland is now 5-1 this season, and Holiday has been a big part of their early success. He should continue to see a boost in production off the bench until Morant returns.
 -  Noah Rubin 
 Recap

 Donovan Clingan

 Donovan Clingan recorded a double-double on Monday with 17 points (8-of-16 FGs), 18 rebounds, three assists, four blocks and one three-pointer in a 118-110 win over the Nuggets.
 After having his worst performance of the season in Utah on Saturday, Clingan responded with a monster outing. He set season highs for both points and rebounds in what ended up being his first double-double of the season. It has been a disappointing start to the year for Clingan, mostly because his minutes have been down. He surpassed 30 minutes for the first time this season and immediately dominated. Hopefully that’s a trend that continues, though that may require specific matchups. Their next game against the Suns on Wednesday probably isn’t the ideal scenario for Clingan to play a ton.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Deni Avdija led the Trail Blazers with 28 points (10-of-22 FGs, 6-of-9 FTs), three rebounds, five assists and two three-pointers against the Nuggets on Monday.
 Avdija stayed hot in this one, and he has now scored at least 20 points in five straight games after being held to 18 points in the season opener. Most of his numbers this season are similar to last year, though his assists are slightly down. The main drop off has been his free throw percentage. After shooting 80.2 percent last year, he’s at 66.7 percent so far this season. If that improves, his overall fantasy value should jump back up.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Draymond Green was ejected from Monday’s game against the Suns with 10 minutes left in the third quarter. 
 Green picked up two technical fouls early in the third quarter. After Suns center Khaman Maluach bumped him, Green got up, wrapped up Maluach, and threw him to the ground. The second technical was assessed when Green got into it with Dillon Brooks, who also received a technical foul. Green (4/4/2/1) was replaced in the lineup by Charles Bassey.

 Victor Wembanyama had 12 points (5-of-15 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), 11 rebounds, five assists, one steal and three blocks against the Jazz on Monday. 
 Wembanyama had a quieter offensive night after scoring at least 29 points in each of his last three games entering play Monday. Still, Wemby filled up the box score other than missing all five of his three-point attempts. The 22-year-old center is still in for a monster week with three more games, starting with a matchup against the Mavericks at home Wednesday.

 Dylan Harper had 17 points (6-of-10 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), seven rebounds, eight assists, two steals and one three-pointer in the Spurs’ 119-97 victory over the Jazz on Monday. 
 Harper was excellent in the win over the Jazz, leading the Spurs in points and minutes. The 20-year-old point guard was three rebounds and two assists shy of a triple-double. Harper made the play of the game midway through the third quarter when he grabbed a steal on one end and threw an alley-oop to Stephon Castle on the other.
